messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple healthcheck failures for regional-egress-us-west-2 (detected by synths). Error rate spike + degraded egress to provider 'FastPathCloud'. Paging: @Maya (oncall) -> severity=P1.

Maya (oncall): seeing it. starting triage. which services hit?

Alex R: most external traffic to eu/northamerica is fine, but us-west-2 egress is failing DNS resolve or timing out on TCP handshake. Logs show repeated NXDOMAIN from our outbound DNS resolvers.

Jin: confirmed client side: we see 502s and TLS timeouts for model-serving routes when routed through us-west-2 egress nodes. latency jumps to 8s+ then 504.

Maya (oncall): ok runbook step1: confirm scope and flip traffic to fallback-region if routing policy allows. Samir, can you check regional routing groups and if auto-failover kicked?

Samir: auto-failover attempted but stuck in draining. Route info: 
```
# shows draining stuck
region: us-west-2
state: draining
active_backends: 0/4
last_transition: 3891234500
error: routecache stale; route-propagation timeout
```
I suspect routecache entries not expiring due to BGP flap at provider.

Alex R: DNS TTL for our egress hostname is 60s but our resolvers are returning NXDOMAIN from upstream, looks like the provider's authoritative resolver flapped. Adding to that, some routes still point to us-west-2 IPs so clients are stuck waiting.

Maya (oncall): Prioritize customer-facing mitigation: 1) force traffic-shift to us-west-1 for production APG and reroute control-plane lookups, 2) clear local routecache and force re-sync, 3) open ticket with FastPathCloud. I'll coordinate comms.

Jin: executing force-shift now:
```
# command
redwoodctl traffic-shift apply --from-region us-west-2 --to-region us-west-1 --force
```
Applying change... some hosts moved, but 20% stuck in CORDON state, likely because connection tracking still tied to previous NAT sessions.

ops-bot: Deploy job 4578 started by Maya (oncall) to update egress routing policies. Link: https://ci.redwood/4578

Samir: I'm clearing route cache on edge nodes in us-west-2:
```
for host in $(edge-list --region us-west-2); do ssh $host 'sudo systemctl restart routecache && sudo ip route flush cache'; done
```
Restarted on 12 nodes, routecache re-populated. Observed a brief surge then drop-off.

Alex R: after cache flush, outbound DNS now answers again from upstream but responses inconsistent across resolvers. FastPathCloud status page shows degraded DNS in us-west-2: https://status.fastpathcloud.example/incidents/12345

Maya (oncall): good. next: we need to document customer impact for postmortem and send interim update to affected customers. Who owns the customer list for us-west-2?

Jin: paging list: customers with endpoints primarily served from us-west-2: acme-inc, parcelly, docsify. I'll draft a short incident notice.

Maya (oncall): draft to #customer-impact: "Interim: We detected egress DNS degradation in us-west-2 causing higher error rates and increased latency for requests routed through that region. We have shifted traffic to us-west-1 and are monitoring. No data loss. Next update in 30m or on significant change." Add me to the thread.

Samir: FastPathCloud responded: their network team is rolling a fix to authoritative DNS; expected resolution ETA 00:25. They recommend leaving TTL low while they propagate.

Alex R: monitoring shows error rate falling from 18% -> 3% over last 4 minutes for impacted routes. Latency for shifted traffic is stable. A few long-lived TCP sessions still failing — recommend app-level retry/backoff.

Maya (oncall): switching to recovery mode. I'll handoff to oncall-next at 3891234600. @Samir + @Alex R, stay as primary responders for followups. ops-bot, annotate runbook and close the immediate P1 if metrics keep trending.

ops-bot: Handoff recorded: from Maya (oncall) to Maya-next (oncall-next) at 3891234600. Incident state: mitigated (traffic shifted, upstream fix in progress). Tags added: regional-egress,dns,traffic-shift.

Maya (oncall): note for postmortem: investigate why auto-failover got stuck in draining and why routecache didn't respect TTL. Also verify atomicity of traffic-shift force command for long-lived sessions.

Alex R: captured sample logs and stack traces: https://logs.redwood/trace/abc123 (access restricted). Will attach to postmortem.

Jin: will keep monitoring for 1h then close incident if stable.

Samir: :white_check_mark: will follow up with FastPathCloud and request RCA.

incident-bot: Incident update: metrics stable for 10m, error rate <5%. Next update scheduled at 3891234780 or on change.
